summary: The kernel assigns a thread to each row below dim, iterates through rowDelimiters[row]..rowDelimiters[row+1], accumulates each stored product and writes out[row]. The runtime iteration count drives repeated launches in compiled host code with synchronization before the timer stops. All four configured architecture variants in the final SASS retain nonzero DFMA paths, CSR-loop backedges, row bounds and output stores.

source_evidence.claim: Thread-to-row guard and full CSR reduction; CLI parses n/s/i, nItems derives matrix density, initialized CSR/value/vector data are copied to device; timed loop launches per iteration, synchronizes, then copies result.
The build targets CUDA architectures 60, 70, 80, and 90 with optimization enabled; these are the SASS variants examined.

compiled_evidence.claim: Clock begins at 1313; runtime count in ebp controls the loop (1318), launch stub is called at 1338 and counter increment/compare/backedge is 1342-1344 to b2d8; device synchronization at 1345 precedes stop clock at 1348.

primary_quality_check.method: Independent full Fable r3 source, timed host flow and complete SASS; Haiku r1 full source, timed host flow and each architecture's cited arithmetic/backedge/store/guard checks. Separately inspected all four Beam timed host loops. Exact-byte comparisons show Beam r2-r5 SASS identical to independently inspected hybrid r1, and Fable r1/r2/r4/r5 SASS identical to r3. Other cases retain the independent Luna source review.
